title: A former OpenAI researcher joins Conduit to pursue non-invasive thought-to-text
friendlyTitle: Conduit wants to turn thoughts into text without surgery
summary: Former OpenAI researcher Naomi Bashkansky joined Conduit to build thought-to-text models trained on non-invasive neural data. Her essay describes the company’s data strategy and an ambitious vision in which neural interfaces become a faster way to communicate intent to AI systems.
friendlySummary: A former OpenAI researcher has joined Conduit to train AI on signals from non-invasive brain sensors.
whyItMatters: Brain-computer interfaces could improve access for people who cannot type or speak and eventually reduce friction when directing assistants. The near-term claims remain speculative, while privacy, consent, security and the reliability of inferred intent will be central product requirements.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This may one day help people communicate with computers more easily, especially when typing or speaking is difficult. It is still early and needs very strong privacy protections.
